players.note: Chase Brown is the RB20 in fantasy points per game just based on volume alone. He has one touchdown all season, and he has averaged 18.5 touches and 75.6 total yards. Brown's role has remained consistent with 75.5% and 68.9% snap rates over the last two games. Overall, he has a 71.4% snap rate with 61.4% of the rushing work, a 57.8% route share, and a 15% target share. Brown has posted a solid 2.21 yards after contact per attempt while also having a disappointing 13% missed tackle rate and 8% explosive run rate. His offensive line hasn't done him many favors with only 1.40 yards before contact per attempt. This week's matchup could finally lead to Brown's first 100-yard day on the ground, though. The Falcons' run defense has fallen off a cliff. In their last five games, they have allowed the fourth-highest explosive run rate, the fifth-highest rushing success rate, the fourth-most yards after contact per attempt, and the 12th-highest missed tackle rate.

Over the last two games, Jonathan Taylor has seen his workload scaled back with a 66.4% snap rate, 44.1% of the rushing work, and a 54.7% route share (15.4% target share). In those games, Taylor has averaged 16 touches and 78.5 total yards. Overall, Taylor has a strong 13.7% explosive run rate and 16% missed tackle rate. Even in a reduced capacity, Taylor should have a nice day against Dallas. Over their last five games, Dallas has allowed the second-most rushing yards over expectation per attempt, the third-most yards before contact per attempt, and the sixth-most yards after contact per attempt.

Rhamondre Stevenson remains New England's workhorse back. Stevenson is the RB22 in fantasy points per game, averaging 14.9 touches and 72.4 total yards. Among 42 qualifying backs, Stevenson is 26th in yards after contact per attempt and seventh in missed tackle rate. Stevenson is a volume-based RB2 again this week. Across their last five games, Green Bay has ranked 15th in rushing success rate while allowing the 12th-most yards after contact per attempt and the tenth-highest missed tackle rate.

Since Caleb Williams' return, Luther Burden has been the WR8 in fantasy points per game with a 20.4% target share, 4.32 YPRR, three red zone targets, a deep target, and a 28.6% first-read share. The only thing that has limited Burden from gaudier numbers is the fact that during that three-game span, he has had only a 56% route share. Burden just shredded Seattle's secondary, so I don't have a ton of concerns about his matchup this week. The Bucs have been quite good against slot receivers, though. Over their last five games, they have allowed the ninth-fewest yards per target to the position while ranking 18th in fantasy points per opportunity. Burden has the talent to overcome another rough-on-paper matchup this week.

Real talk time. Parker Washington is damn good and has had a bad run, with the Jags blowing out teams. I'm not panicking at all on Washington. Last week, they crushed the Jags while Trevor Lawrence had to throw the ball only 14 times. Against Houston, Washington earned 11 targets and dropped a touchdown. Even going back to the game against Cincy, Washington had to deal with DJ Turner for most of the game, so the disappearing act is understandable. Ok. Rant over. Washington is the WR22 in fantasy points per game with a 22.9% target share (leads the team), 2.47 YPRR, seven red zone targets (leads the team), nine deep targets (leads the team), and a 26.6% first-read share (leads the team). So, just to recap, Washington leads the team in every important metric for pass catchers. This week, Washington gets to face a Baltimore secondary that, over their last five games, has allowed the most yards per target and the ninth-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Rashee Rice returned to the lineup last week and was the WR9 in weekly scoring. Rice had a 19.5% target share with 1.89 YPRR (53 receiving yards), one red zone target, and a 27.6% first-read share. Rice returned to his low aDOT role with a 4.25 aDOT and a 37.5% designed target rate. Rice could continue the strong production in his old role this week. Since Week 5, the Jets have had the 12th-highest rate of single high (54.5%). Against single high, Rice has had a 22% TPRR with 2.10 YPRR. Over their last five games, the Jets have allowed the 12th-most yards per target and the fourth-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

In Week 7, Jonah Coleman led the backfield in snaps (50%), rushing attempts (nine, 34.6%), and was second in route share (21.9%), running one less route than RJ Harvey. Coleman finished with 11 touches and 69 total yards. Last week, his role grew further with RJ Harvey out. Coleman finished with 15 touches and 104 total yards (RB12 for the week) with a 67.9% snap rate, a 47.8% rushing share, and a 50% route share (12.5% target share). This season, among 58 qualifying rushers, Coleman is first in explosive run rate and 19th in missed tackle rate. Coleman is a wonderful fantasy option this week, and he could continue to crush. Over their last five games, Carolina has allowed the tenth-highest explosive run rate, the ninth-highest yards before contact per attempt, and the fourth-highest missed tackle rate.

I'll lead this conversation with I don't know if Patrick Surtain shadows anyone this week. He didn't shadow last week, and I could easily see him not following anyone this week. Tetairoa McMillan is the WR14 in fantasy points per game, but with Bryce Young struggling he hasn't managed more than 11.8 PPR points in each of the last two weeks. McMIllan has a 22.6% target share with 2.14 YPRR, six red zone targets, eight deep targets, and a 32.7% first-read share. McMillan could see solid volume this week, but I worry about his floor and ceiling against Denver in a game where I worry that we will see Young struggle again. Over the last five games, Denver has allowed the seventh-fewest yards per target and the fourth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Since Week 4, Ollie Gordon has been the RB16 in fantasy points per game, averaging 18.6 touches and 90 total yards. Among 42 qualifying backs, Gordon is eighth in explosive run rate and 23rd in yards after contact per attempt. The only drawback to Gordon has been the lack of passing game involvement. Over his last four games, he has only six targets and zero receiving yards. He has to get it done on early downs, which he has been doing. Gordon will find more uphill sledding this week, though. Over their last five games, Detroit has allowed the eighth-lowest rushing success rate, the fewest yards after contact per attempt, and the 12th-fewest rushing yards over expectation per attempt. He'll need a touchdown to pay off for fantasy this week, along with all the volume he can handle.

Since Week 6, as the starting back for Houston, Woody Marks has been the RB35 in fantasy points per game, averaging 18.5 touches and 74.3 total yards. With that type of volume, the biggest culprit for underperforming in fantasy is the fact that he didn't have a touchdown in either game. In those two games, he played 83.2% of the snaps with 68% of the rushing work and a 56.9% route share (6.5% target share). Among 42 qualifying backs, he is 21st in explosive run rate and 18th in missed tackle rate. Marks is a volume-based RB2 with a good matchup this week. Over their last five games, the Bolts have allowed the eighth-highest explosive run rate, the sixth-most rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the tenth-most yards after contact per attempt.

As I started my discussion about Tetairoa McMillan, I'll lead this conversation with I don't know if Patrick Surtain shadows anyone this week. He didn't shadow last week, and I could easily see him not following anyone this week. Jalen Coker is the WR24 in fantasy points per game. Over the last two games, with Bryce Young falling apart, Coker has had 1.9 and 9.6 PPR points, and that latter mark was fueled by one big play and a touchdown. Coker has a 17.2% target share with 1.98 YPRR, six red zone targets, ten deep targets, and a 25.8% first-read share. I have serious concerns that Young will struggle again this week which drastically lowers Coker's ceiling and floor against Denver. This is also a tough matchup for Coker. Over the last five games, Denver has allowed the seventh-fewest yards per target and the fourth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Last week, Quinshon Judkins had a season-low 39.1% snap rate with 73.3% of the rushing work and only an 18% route share (4.9% target share). In the first seven weeks of the season, Judkins had a 59.2% snap rate and a 30.3% route share. We'll see if this role reduction holds this week, but it's a worry for Judkins moving forward. Judkins is the RB23 in fantasy points per game, averaging 15.4 touches and 68 total yards. Among 45 qualifying backs, he is 37th in explosive run rate, 39th in yards after contact per attempt, and 32nd in missed tackle rate. If the Browns play with a lead this week, they could load up Judkins with rushing volume. If that happens, he'll have a nice stat line. The Saints have been unable to stop the run. Over their last five games, they have allowed the seventh-highest rushing success rate, the fifth-most rushing yards over expectation per attempt, the seventh-most yards after contact per attempt, and the 13th-highest missed tackle rate.

Derrick Henry might be the RB13 in fantasy points per game overall, but that doesn't tell the entire story. Since Week 4, without Lamar Jackson, he has been the RB28 in fantasy points per game, averaging 19.8 touches and 73.6 total yards. Among 42 qualifying backs, he is still performing well, ranking 18th in explosive run rate and 17th in yards after contact per attempt. Henry is now a volume-based RB2 with a horrible matchup this week. Yes, Jacksonville just lost DaVon Hamilton, but they should still field a solid, if not strong, run defense. Over their last five games, the Jags have allowed the third-lowest explosive run rate, the lowest rushing success rate, and the third-lowest missed tackle rate.

Jameson Williams has been on a heater. After last week's game, he has risen to the WR18 in fantasy points per game. Since Week 4, Williams has been the WR8 in fantasy points per game with a 19.4% target share, 2.40 YPRR, seven red zone targets, eight deep targets, and a 27.7% first-read share. Williams should roast the Dolphins' secondary. Over their last five games, Miami has allowed the sixth-most yards per target and the third-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Last week, Saquon Barkley played only 32.4% of the snaps with a 44.8% rushing share and a 16.3% route share (2.9% target share). Last week, Barkley finished with 14 touches and 54 total yards (one touchdown). Barkley was the RB22 in weekly scoring. In the last two weeks, Barkley has had an 11.8% explosive run rate, 2.55 yards after contact per attempt, and a 20% missed tackle rate. These are all amazing numbers considering Barkley has been playing with one healthy leg and a balky back. Barkley can get it done this week on limited volume. Over the last five games, New York has allowed the seventh-highest explosive run rate, the ninth-most rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the 15th-most yards after contact per attempt. Barkley opened the week with a DNP.

Sam LaPorta has been quiet over the last two games with only 51 total receiving yards, but this is the eruption spot for LaPorta. Sammy Ballgame is the TE6 in fantasy points per game. LaPorta has a 15.7% target share with 1.72 YPRR, nine red zone targets, one deep target, and a 16.6% first-read share. Over their last five games, Miami has allowed the ninth-most yards per target, the second-most receiving touchdowns, and the third-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Last week, Ashton Jeanty was turned into the passing-down-only back with a 36.7% snap rate, only two rushing attempts, a 48.1% route share, and an 11.5% target share. I don't know if this is the beginning of a new role for him or punishment for mouthing off to the media about the Jets' run defense. We'll have to wait and see what his usage looks like in Week 9. In Weeks 1-7, Jeanty had a 69.5% snap rate, 60.9% of the rushing work, and a 54.8% route share (16.5% target share). Last week, Jeanty finished with five touches and 73 total yards. In Weeks 1-7, Jeanty averaged 20 touches and 91.5 total yards (RB14 in fantasy points per game). This season, Jeanty has 2.13 yards after contact per attempt, which is solid, but he has also logged a 12% missed tackle rate and 5.1% explosive run rate. Those last two stats won't get it done, but we also have to remember he has been playing through injury and behind an offensive line that has been putrid. The Raiders rank dead last in yards before contact per attempt (0.97). The Packers are 31st, and they have generated 1.28 yards before contact per attempt just for context. Jeanty has a wide range of outcomes this week, but even if his previous role comes back, he has a tough matchup. Over their last five games, the 49ers have allowed the lowest explosive run rate, the second-lowest yards after contact per attempt, and the seventh-lowest missed tackle rate.

Overall, Stefon Diggs is the WR20 in fantasy points per game. Over the last two games, Diggs has had an 18.8% target share (leads the team) with 1.46 YPRR, two red zone targets, one deep target, and a 23.4% first-read share (leads the team). The Rams have the fifth-highest two-high rate (62.2%). Over the last two games, against two high, Diggs has had a 17% TPRR with 0.50 YPRR. Overall this season, against two high, Diggs has a 30% TPRR with 1.27 YPRR. Those numbers aren't amazing, but the Rams have been allowing production to slot receivers. They could help boost Diggs' lagging effectiveness against two high. Over their last five games, the Rams have ranked 15th in yards per target against slot receivers while allowing the sixth-most fantasy points per opportunity to the position.

In Weeks 4-8, without Lamar Jackson under center for the majority of games, Zay Flowers has been the WR14 in fantasy points per game with two 100-yard receiving days. In those games, Flowers has had a 28.3% target share with 2.31 YPRR, four red zone targets, four deep targets, and a 35.5% first-read share. There are obvious quarterback play concerns with Baltimore now that could persist for the rest of the season. Flowers can still rely on volume weekly, but his range of outcomes is much wider. This week, he'll need all the volume possible. Over their last five games, the Jags have allowed the seventh-fewest yards per target and the 12th-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers.

DJ Moore continues to battle through a gimpy shoulder. In his three full games, he has commanded elite usage with a 27% target share and 25.9% first-read share with 3.23 YPRR, four red zone targets, and five deep targets. In those three games, Moore finished as the WR9, WR30, and the WR13 in weekly scoring. This week, he faces a tough matchup. Over their last five games, Minnesota has held perimeter wide receivers to the fewest yards per target and the third-fewest fantasy points per opportunity. Moore will need a healthy dose of volume and a touchdown to overcome the rough matchup this week.

Tyler Warren is the TE5 in fantasy points per game. Warren has a 22.3% target share with 1.26 YPRR, five red zone targets, zero deep targets, and a 21.8% first-read share. He'll need a touchdown this week to finish as a TE1 because one of the few things Dallas has been doing well is defending tight ends. Over their last five games, they have allowed the seventh-fewest yards per target and the eighth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to the position.

After last week's monster game, Harold Fannin is the TE8 in fantasy points per game. Fannin has a 19.1% target share with 1.72 YPRR, four red zone targets, two deep targets, and a 19.6% first-read share. This week, he'll face a Saints defense that has the second-highest single high rate in the NFL (65%). Against single-high, Fannin has a 22% TPRR (second on the team) with 1.91 YPRR. Fannin should post another strong TE1 stat line this week. Over their last five games, New Orleans has allowed the sixth-most yards per target and the fifth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Michael Wilson practiced in a limited fashion all week (ribs). He doesn't carry an injury designation into Week 9. After a big game last week, Wilson is the WR22 in fantasy points per game. Wilson has a 23.4% target share with 1.57 YPRR, 15 red zone targets, 16 deep targets, and a 30% first-read share. Wilson has been a volume hog. This week, he could struggle, though. Seattle has the seventh-highest two-high rate in the NFL (60%). Against two-high, Wilson has seen his productivity wane with only an 18% TPRR and 1.12 YPRR. Seattle's secondary has taken a step back over the last five games, allowing the 11th-most yards per target to perimeter wide receivers while ranking 17th in fantasy points per opportunity against the position. Wilson is a volume-based WR3/flex this week.

Last week, Jeremiyah Love and Bam Knight got injured, and Tyler Allgeier became the team's bell-cow runner against Dallas. Allgeier responded with 16 touches and 191 total yards (two scores) as the RB1 for the week. I don't expect that type of output from Allgeier moving forward, especially this week, but he will be a volume-fueled running back option for lineups. Among 42 qualifying backs, Allgeier is first in yards after contact per attempt and 31st in missed tackle rate. This week, he'll need all the volume he can handle and a touchdown to pay off for fantasy. Seattle has shut down rushers. Over their last five games, they have allowed the fourth-lowest explosive run rate, the 11th-lowest rushing success rate, and the eighth-fewest yards before contact per attempt.

Travis Kelce keeps motoring along as a low-end TE1 as the TE11 in fantasy points per game. Kelce has a 17.7% target share with 2.23 YPRR, three red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 20% first-read share. Kelce has had at least 50 receiving yards in five of seven games this season. Kelce should produce as a TE1 again this week. Over the last five games, New York has allowed the 11th-most yards per target and the 12th-most fantasy points per opportunity (tied) to tight ends.

Jaylen Waddle is the WR42 in fantasy points per game, with only three games this season with 14 or more PPR points. Bo Nix has crushed him. Waddle has an 18.8% target share with 1.62 YPRR, four red zone targets, eight deep targets, and a 28.6% first-read share. This week, he faces a pass defense that has the fifth-highest single high rate (59.3%). Against single high, Waddle has had a 31% TPRR (leads the team) with 1.56 YPRR. Waddle could post a strong stat line this week if Nix can get him the ball. Over their last five games, Carolina has allowed the tenth-most yards per target and receiving fantasy points per game to perimeter wide receivers.

Last week, Rachaad White had to deal with Jeremy McNichols and Austin Ekeler cutting into his workload. With McNichols placed on IR, White will likely only have to deal with Ekeler this week, but Robert Henry Jr. could get into the mix, and I wouldn't be shocked. Last week, White played 47.4% of the snaps with 42.3% of the rushing work and a 39.4% route share (10.3% target share). White finished with 12 touches and 60 total yards (one score) as the RB15 for the week. White has posted a solid 17% missed tackle rate this season but a disappointing 1.87 yards after contact per attempt. White will need to make the most of his volume and likely get into the endzone to pay off for fantasy this week. The matchup is rough. The Rams' run defense has improved. Over the last five games, they have allowed the 13th-lowest rushing success rate, the 11th-lowest rushing yards over expectation per attempt, the fourth-lowest yards after contact per attempt, and the sixth-lowest missed tackle rate.

In the two games this season in which Ladd McConkey has played more than 50% of the snaps, he has had a 15.2% target share with 2.34 YPRR, zero red zone targets, three deep targets, and an 18.9% first-read share. Houston has the sixth-highest single high rate (59.1%). This season against single-high, McConkey has had a strong 24% TPRR with 2.83 YPRR. This could be the game where he finally breaks out. Across their last five games, the Texans have allowed the ninth-most yards per target and receiving fantasy points per game.

Denzel Boston is the WR37 in fantasy points per game with a 20.3% target share, 1.57 YPRR, eight red zone targets, 15 deep targets, and a 24.4% first-read share. Boston has been relatively quiet over the last few weeks. He hasn't managed more than 46 receiving yards in any game since Week 4 and hasn't scored a touchdown since Week 5. This week, he'll face a Saints defense that has the second-highest single high rate in the NFL (65%). Against single high, Boston has only a 15% TPRR with a minuscule 0.57 YPRR. The coverage matchup isn't in his favor, and the corners have been good for the Saints on the perimeter. Over their last five games, New Orleans has allowed the 13th-fewest yards per target and the seventh-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to the position. Sit Boston this week.

T.J. Hockenson is the TE10 in fantasy points per game. Hockenson has an 18.7% target share with 2.22 YPRR, seven red zone targets, and a 20.6% first-read share. He could easily be a TE1 again this week against a defense that, over its last five games, has allowed the fifth-most yards per target to tight ends.

KC Concepcion is the WR56 in fantasy points per game. Concepcion had a blow-up game against the Titans, but unfortunately he followed it up with a quieter outing last week against the Steelers. Concepcion has an 18.2% target share with 1.57 YPRR, three red zone targets, five deep targets, and a 25% first-read share (leads the team). This week, he'll face a Saints defense that has the second-highest single high rate in the NFL (65%). Against single high, Concepcion leads the team with a 23% TPRR while posting 1.73 YPRR. The Saints have been ripped apart by slot receivers. Over their last five games, they have allowed the highest yards per target, the ninth-most receiving fantasy points per game, and the third-most fantasy points per opportunity to the position.

Keenan Allen is the WR38 in fantasy points per game, with three weeks this season with at least 13 PPR points. Allen has a 21.2% target share with 1.80 YPRR, four red zone targets, two deep targets, and a 26.2% first-read share. Allen is a viable flex option again this week. Over their last five games, Dallas has allowed the sixth-most receiving fantasy points per game and the 11th-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Since Week 5, Kyle Pitts has been the TE6 in fantasy points per game. In those four games, Pitts has had a 66.9% route share, a 17.5% target share, 1.40 YPRR, six red zone targets, and a 21.2% first-read share. Cincy still can't stop tight ends. They have been hopeless against them, which makes Pitts a strong start this week with huge upside. In their last five games, Cincy has allowed the most yards per target and the second-most receiving yards to tight ends.

After two monstrous games, Omar Cooper was held without a target last week despite his 74.3% route share. Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchel stole the show. In the two previous games, Cooper was the WR6 and WR9 in weekly scoring. In those games, Cooper had a 20% target share, 4.45 YPRR, two red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 29.3% first-read share. Kansas City has the sixth-highest two-high rate in the NFL (59.3%). Since Week 6, against two-high, Cooper has had a 15% TPRR and 1.76 YPRR. Cooper could operate as New York's WR1 this week. With a middle-of-the-road matchup in the slot this week, Cooper could see a heavy workload. Over their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the 14th-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers while ranking 16th in yards per target.

Since Caleb Williams' return, Rome Odunze has been the WR43 in fantasy points per game with a 13.6% target share, 2.03 YPRR, one red zone target, four deep targets, and a 14.3% first-read share. Odunze has been squeezed for targets, with Colston Loveland operating as the alpha and Luther Burden as the number two option. Sit Odunze this week. Over their last five games, the Bucs have allowed the 12th-fewest yards per target and the sixth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Breece Hall will be back this week. With that said, I don't know what to do with the Jets backfield. I can envision an easy scenario where Hall is immediately reinstalled as the Jets' workhorse this week, but I can also understand if New York wants to deploy a committee or have a hot hand approach this week. Braelon Allen was absolutely awesome with Hall out, so it's likely tough to put that tackle-breaking genie back in the bottle. Among 42 qualifying backs, Hall is 20th in explosive run rate, 41st in yards after contact per attempt, and 27th in missed tackle rate. Hall hasn't been immensely efficient with his workload this season even before dealing with the injury. With workload questions this week, Hall needs to be as efficient as possible with his touches, but that will be tough against the Chiefs' stout run defense. Over their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the eighth-lowest explosive run rate, the fifth-lowest rushing success rate, and the second-lowest rushing yards over expectation per attempt. Hall could be a volume-based RB2 this week or a touchdown-needy RB3/flex.

After a slow start, since Week 4, Tucker Kraft has been the TE6 in fantasy points per game. Since Week 4, Kraft has had a 70.8% route share, a 17% target share, 1.77 YPRR, eight red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 20% first-read share. Kraft isn't likely to have a blow-up game this week, but with his touchdown equity in the Packers' passing attack, he could easily be a solid TE1. Over their last five games, New England has allowed the 11th-most receiving fantasy points per game and ranked 18th in yards per target against tight ends.

Tre Tucker is the WR25 in fantasy points per game, with three games with at least 18.8 PPR points this season. Tucker has a 16.4% target share with 2.03 YPRR, six red zone targets, nine deep targets, and a 21.7% first-read share. Since Week 6, the 49ers have had the fifth-highest single-high rate (62.2%). Against single-high, Tucker has had a 20% TPRR and 2.01 YPRR. The coverage matchup is in his favor in the sense that Tucker excels against both single and two high, but as far as his downfield role, I don't think he'll have success there. 31.4% of his receiving yardage has been via deep targets, but over their last five games the 49ers have held passers to the 14th-lowest passing success rate and passer rating when targeting 20-plus yards downfield. Also, over their last five games, the 49ers have held perimeter wide receivers to the tenth-fewest yards per target while ranking 15th in fantasy points per opportunity. Sit Tucker this week.

Malik Washington has been a volume-filled flex this season as the WR40 in fantasy points per game. Last week, Washington finally got into the end zone and finished as the WR14 for the week. Washington has a 24.6% target share with 1.81 YPRR, three red zone targets, nine deep targets, and a 27.1% first-read share. This week, he'll face a Lions' secondary that has the eighth-highest single-high rate (57.3%). Against single-high, Washington leads the team with a 23% TPRR and 2.03 YPRR. Washington is a volume-based flex again this week, but the matchup isn't ideal. Over their last five games, Detroit has allowed the fifth-most receiving fantasy points per game to slot receivers while holding them to the 11th-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.

Over the last two weeks, Caleb Douglas has had a 15.1% target share, 2.31 YPRR, one red zone target, one deep target, and a 20.6% first-read share. Douglas has had plenty of flashes when on the field, with a 70-yard and two-touchdown outing against the Jets and 94 receiving yards earlier this season against the Raiders. This week, he'll face a Lions' secondary that has the eighth-highest single-high rate (57.3%). Against single high, Douglas is second on the team with a 23% TPRR and 2.00 YPRR. Douglas is flex-viable, but Detroit has been tougher against perimeter wide receivers in recent weeks. Over their last five games, Detroit has held perimeter wide receivers to the 11th-fewest yards per target and fantasy points per opportunity.

Blake Corum is on fire! Since Week 5, he has been the RB13 in fantasy points per game, averaging 12 touches and 76.6 total yards. Corum has scored a touchdown in each of his last four games. Among 42 qualifying backs, Corum is seventh in explosive run rate and 17th in missed tackle rate. This could be the week that Corum's hot streak ends, though. Over their last five games, Washington has tightened up the run defense, allowing the fifth-lowest explosive run rate, the sixth-fewest yards before contact per attempt, and the third-lowest missed tackle rate.

Since Week 6, Makai Lemon has been the WR31 in fantasy points per game. In the last three weeks, Lemon has had an 18.4% target share with 1.22 YPRR, one red zone target, one deep target, and a 22.7% first-read share. This isn't the week to expect much from Lemon as a flex, though. Over the last five games, the Giants have shut down slot receivers, allowing the fifth-fewest yards per target and the fourth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.

Last week, Adonai Mitchell was still just a part-time player with a 60.7% snap rate and 71.4% route share. He made the most of his routes with a 28.1% target share (24.6 aDOT), seven receptions, 142 receiving yards, one red zone target, five deep targets, and a 31% first-read share. Mitchell might log back-to-back strong weeks if Geno Smith is willing to test Kansas City's pass defense downfield. With Garrett Wilson out, he could also see a bump in his playing time and usage. The Chiefs have allowed the second-highest passer rating and the third-highest success rate to deep passing this season. Over their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the ninth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers while ranking 17th in yards per target. The matchup isn't ideal, but if Mitchell connects on a handful of deep targets, he could be a nice flex this week.

Last week, Jadarian Price surprisingly led the backfield with a 48.2% snap rate, a 52.6% rushing share, and a 33.3% route share. Price finished with 12 touches and 37 total yards. The red zone work was split up between Price and Zach Charbonnet, with Price seeing one carry inside the 20-yard line while Charbonnet had two. Price has been efficient with his workload this season with 2.55 yards after contact per attempt and a 24% missed tackle rate. I have no clue if he'll continue to lead the way for Seattle's ground game, though. That was Zach Charbonnet's first game back in the lineup, and I expect his role to grow moving forward. Price will need volume this week and a score to pay off as a flex this week. Arizona's run defense has massively improved. Over their last five games, they have allowed the sixth-lowest explosive run rate, the sixth-lowest rushing success rate, and the seventh-fewest yards after contact per attempt.

Josh Downs is the WR55 in fantasy points per game. Last week, he saved his fantasy day with a score, but it was his fifth game in a row without surpassing 50 receiving yards. Downs has a 17.8% target share with 1.25 YPRR, six red zone targets, eight deep targets, and a 21.9% first-read share. The biggest plus for Downs this week is how bad Dallas has been at defending the slot. Over their last five games, Dallas has allowed the third-most yards per target and the 11th-most fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers. Downs is a decent flex option based on the matchup.

Dalton Kincaid is the TE8 in fantasy points per game. He had a big bounce-back game last week as the TE4 for the week. That was the first game he had crossed 12 PPR points since Week 2. Overall, he has a 61.6% route share, a 17.1% target share, 2.75 YPRR, six red zone targets, five deep targets, and a 21.4% first-read share. This feels like another down week incoming for Kincaid. This week, he'll face a Vikings secondary that has the fourth-highest two-high rate in the NFL (64%). Against two-high, Kincaid has a 20% TPRR with 1.44 YPRR. Over their last five games, Minnesota has allowed the fourth-fewest yards per target and the fewest fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

In the Saints' pass-happy offense, Devaughn Vele is the WR29 in fantasy points per game with a 16.5% target share, 1.33 YPRR, six red zone targets, eight deep targets, and a 21.2% first-read share. Vele has at least 50 receiving yards and a score in three games this season. This week, he'll face a Browns defense that has the highest single high rate in the NFL (75.7%). Against single-high, Vele has seen his TPRR increase from 15% to 20% and his YPRR jump to 2.02. Vele is a strong flex again this week. Over their last five games, Cleveland has allowed the 11th-most yards per target and receiving fantasy points per game to slot receivers.

Since Week 5, Alvin Kamara has had a 36.9% snap rate, 22.2% of the rushing work, and a 32.3% route share (14% target share). Since Week 5, he has averaged nine touches and 45.7 total yards. In those three games, he has had a 12.5% explosive run rate, 2.19 yards after contact per attempt, and a 31% missed tackle rate. Those numbers imply Kamara is getting healthier because he hasn't posted numbers like that until this point in the season. Kamara could surprise with a strong showing this week. The Browns have been bleeding out production to backs. Over their last five games, they have allowed the second-highest explosive run rate, the eighth-highest rushing success rate, and the second-highest yards after contact per attempt and missed tackle rate.

After last week's limited volume performance, Brenton Strange has fallen to TE15 in fantasy points per game. Strange has a 17.4% target share with 2.26 YPRR, three red zone targets, one deep target, and an 18.9% first-read share. Strange could easily bounce back this week as a strong TE1. Over their last five games, Baltimore has allowed the 14th-most yards per target and the fourth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Since Week 6, Dallas Goedert has been the TE19 in fantasy points per game. Goedert has had a 15.4% target share with 1.65 YPRR, one red zone target, and a 24% first-read share. This week he's a must-sit. Over their last five games, the Giants have held tight ends to the third-fewest yards per target and the seventh-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.

Braelon Allen could immediately return to operating as Breece Hall's understudy, or he could force a committee. Allen was fantastic with Hall out. In Weeks 4-8, Allen averaged 21.2 touches and 114.8 total yards as the RB15 in fantasy points per game. Among 42 qualifying backs, Allen is third in explosive run rate, seventh in yards after contact per attempt, and 14th in missed tackle rate. If the Jets open Week 9 with a hot hand approach with their backfield, don't be surprised if Allen has the warmer mitts. Allen's range of outcomes is wide. He could be a decent RB2 or a touchdown-needy flex this week. Over their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the eighth-lowest explosive run rate, the fifth-lowest rushing success rate, and the second-lowest rushing yards over expectation per attempt.

Since Week 5, with Justin Jefferson in the lineup and Kyler Murray under center, Jordan Addison has been the WR56 in fantasy points per game. During that stretch, he has had a 20.8% target share with 1.54 YPRR, zero red zone targets, five deep targets, and a 25.6% first-read share. In those two games, Addison surpassed 50 receiving yards once. Addison is a decent flex this week with a good matchup. Over their last five games, Buffalo has allowed the third-most yards per target and the fifth-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

It looks like Emeka Egbuka will be back this week. After opening the week with a DNP, he followed it up with full practices on Thursday and Friday. The Bucs have not wanted to throw the ball the last two games due to weather concerns and Baker Mayfield's ailing thumb. Maybe that changes this week, as they will likely be playing catch-up with the Bears leading. Egbuka is the WR32 in fantasy points per game with a 25.3% target share, 1.19 YPRR, six red zone targets, six deep targets, and a 31.7% first-read share. Egbuka could turn in a nice stat line this week if Mayfield can deliver catchable targets. Over their last five games, the Bears have allowed the fourth-most yards per target and the most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Jakobi Meyers is the WR51 in fantasy points per game with three outings this season with 12.2 or more PPR points. Meyers has a 15.4% target share with 1.85 YPRR, seven red zone targets (tied for the team lead), three deep targets, and a 17.5% first-read share. Meyers is a solid flex again this week. Over their last five games, Baltimore has allowed the most yards per target and the ninth-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Since Week 5, Ryan Flournoy has been the WR29 in fantasy points per game. In those four games, he has had a 13.8% target share with 1.90 YPRR, four red zone targets, one deep target, and a 12.1% first-read share. Flournoy is in place as a flex again this week, but the matchup isn't as kind as last week. Over their last five games, Indy has allowed the ninth-fewest yards per target and the 13th-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Since Week 4, Khalil Shakir has been a dependable, low-ceiling weekly PPR flex as the WR32 in fantasy points per game. In each of those games, he scored between 11 and 13.4 PPR points. Since Week 4, he has had an 18.5% target share with 2.55 YPRR, three red zone targets, one deep target, and a 21% first-read share. This week, he'll face a Vikings secondary that has the fourth-highest two-high rate in the NFL (64%). Against two high, Shakir has a 23% TPRR and 2.14 YPRR. Josh Allen could lean on Shakir this week. Minnesota has been more giving to the slot. Over their last five games, they have allowed the 11th-most yards per target while ranking 15th in fantasy points per opportunity allowed to the position. Another feather in Shakir's cap is how much his production has spiked when Josh Allen has been blitzed. Minnesota leads the NFL with a 74.2% blitz rate. Against the blitz, Shakir has seen his TPRR jump from 19% to 29% and his YPRR sky rocket from 1.37 to 3.63 (WOW!). Shakir could cook this week.

Last week was Zach Charbonnet's first game back. Charbonnet finished with nine touches and 29 total yards while leading the backfield with two red zone rushing attempts. Charbonnet was second on the team in backfield snap rate (35.7%), rushing share (31.6%), and route share (17.9%). He has only 1.67 yards after contact per attempt but a solid 17% missed tackle rate. Charbonnet's workload is likely to grow moving forward, but I don't want to flex him this week. Arizona's run defense has massively improved. Over their last five games, they have allowed the sixth-lowest explosive run rate, the sixth-lowest rushing success rate, and the seventh-fewest yards after contact per attempt.

Devin Singletary should operate as the Giants' workhorse this week, with only Singletary and Greg Desrosiers healthy in the running back room. This season, in limited duty, Singletary has posted a solid 2.11 yards after contact per attempt and a 17% missed tackle rate. He should flirt with 15-18 touches this week with a nice matchup incoming. Singletary is an RB2 this week. Over the last five games, Philly's run defense has been leaky, allowing the 11th-highest explosive run rate, the sixth-highest rushing success rate, the eighth-highest yards after contact per attempt, and the seventh-highest missed tackle rate.

When Rashee Rice has been a full-time player, Xavier Worthy has had a 15.1% target share with 0.62 YPRR, six red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 19.4% first-read share. He hasn't surpassed 25 receiving yards in any of those four games. I don't have any faith left in Worthy. I understand he surpassed 70 receiving yards against the Raiders and Chargers' secondaries with Rice out, but with Rice in the lineup, he has been a ghost. Since Week 5, the Jets have had the 12th-highest rate of single-high (54.5%). Against single-high, Worthy has had a 22% TPRR, but he has only produced 0.88 YPRR. The Jets' secondary has been giving, but this might be asking too much of them to hoist up Worthy to a productive Week 9. Over their last five games, the Jets have allowed the 12th-most yards per target and the fourth-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Greg Dulcich has emerged as a big part of the Miami passing offense over his last three games. Since Week 5, Dulcich has had a 62.6% route share, a 20% target share, 2.68 YPRR, two red zone targets, one deep target, and a 25.5% first-read share. Dulcich is a wonderful streaming option this week, and he could be a TE1 this week. Over their last five games, Detroit has allowed the third-most yards per target, the most receiving fantasy points per game, and the most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Over the last two weeks, Aaron Jones has been a committee back with Jordan Mason, averaging eight touches and 33 total yards. In those games, he has had a 32.1% snap rate, 27.7% of the rushing attempts, and a 21% route share. Mason has bested him in each of those categories as Minny's lead back. Jones has shown his age this season with only 1.97 yards after contact per attempt and a 12% missed tackle rate. He's a touchdown-dependent flex this week. Over their last five games, the Bills have allowed the 12th-highest explosive run rate and rushing success rate and the sixth-highest missed tackle rate.

This has been a lost season for Courtland Sutton as the WR80 in fantasy points per game. Sutton hasn't managed double-digit PPR points this season in any week. Sutton has a 14% target share with 1.07 YPRR, seven red zone targets, six deep targets, and a 20.7% first-read share. This week, he faces a pass defense that has the fifth-highest single high rate (59.3%). Against single high, Sutton has a 22% TPRR and 1.19 YPRR. Nix has enough trouble supporting Jaylen Waddle weekly, much less anyone else. Sutton is a deep league flex only. Over their last five games, Carolina has allowed the tenth-most yards per target and receiving fantasy points per game to perimeter wide receivers.

Over the last two games, Jordan Mason has been the Vikings' lead back, averaging only 12.5 touches and 44 total yards. Mason has had a 46.2% snap rate, 48.9% of the rushing work, and a 24.2% route share. He has led the Minny backfield in each of those categories over the last two games. Mason has posted a disappointing 1.89 yards after contact per attempt and an 8% missed tackle rate this season. With the limited volume and effectiveness, Mason is a touchdown-dependent flex this week. Over their last five games, the Bills have allowed the 12th-highest explosive run rate and rushing success rate, and the sixth-highest missed tackle rate.

Mike Gesicki is the TE12 in fantasy points per game. Overall, he has a 47.8% snap rate, a 54.7% route share, a 9% target share, 1.53 YPRR, five red zone targets, two deep targets, and an 11.1% first-read share. What has propped up his fantasy value is his insane touchdown runout, as he has six scores this season. Last week, without Erick All, Gesicki did see a jump in his playing time with a 71.7% route share and 67.1% snap rate. I expect those numbers to carry over into Week 9. Gesicki is an interesting streaming option this week. The coverage matchup is in his favor, but Atlanta has been tough against tight ends, so he has a wide range of outcomes this week. Atlanta has the third-highest rate of single high (60.7%). Against single-high, Gesicki has seen his TPRR increase to 20% with 2.00 YPRR. However, over their last five games, Atlanta has allowed the 11th-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends while ranking 16th in yards per target. Gesicki could be a TE1 this week or disappoint. It's a coin flip.

Since Week 6, Chig Okonkwo has been the TE21 in fantasy points per game with one TE1 outing (TE11). In those two games, Okonkwo has had a 15.9% target share with 1.58 YPRR, one red zone target, one deep target, and a 21.3% first-read share. This isn't the matchup to consider streaming Okonkwo. Over their last five games, the Rams have held tight ends to the 11th-fewest yards per target and the sixth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.

The Bucs have leaned extremely run-heavy over the last two games. In that span, Kenneth Gainwell has averaged 19.5 carries and 114 rushing yards as the RB35 in fantasy points per game. Gainwell has been awesome on a per-touch basis this season with a 15.5% explosive run rate, 3.09 yards after contact per attempt, and a 29% missed tackle rate. We'll see if the Bucs continue this run-centric offense in Week 9 or if the Bears can pry them away from it, but Gainwell is still a solid flex this week. Last week, the Bears' run defense looked like a force, with Jeffery Simmons clogging up the middle. They allowed only a 26.3% rushing success rate, -0.57 rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and 1.68 yards after contact per attempt. Gainwell won't have an easy road this week, but if he gets 10-15 touches, he can still be flex-worthy.

Juwan Johnson has seen his role decline. In his last two games, Johnson has had only a 56.8% snap rate, 56.2% route share, 4.4% target share, and a 7% first-read share. Over their last five games, Cleveland has ranked 15th in receiving fantasy points per game against tight ends while giving up the 12th-most fantasy points per opportunity to the position. This would put Johnson on the streaming radar this week, but I'm not starting him in most formats. I need to see his role rebound before I'm comfortable plugging him into a starting lineup.

Last week was just more of the same for Omarion Hampton. He finished with 11 touches and 27 total yards. He had only a 30.5% snap rate, 36% of the rushing work, and an 18.9% route share. If any player not named Omarion Hampton had this lengthy resume of underperformance entering Week 9, he'd be dropped in every league. Hampton has a decent 2.33 yards after contact per attempt, but his 8.6% explosive run rate and 13% missed tackle rate are eye sores. This is another week to sit Hampton. Over their last five games, Houston has allowed the seventh-lowest explosive run rate, the 12th-fewest rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the 14th-fewest yards after contact per attempt.

Mike Washington took over as the team's lead back last week, but I don't know how long that will last. The workload could easily bounce back in the direction of Ashton Jeanty this week if this were all related to his quotes about the Jets' run defense. I have no clue if it's related, but we'll find out how this all shakes out this week. In Weeks 1-7, Washington had a 20.9% snap rate, averaging 6.1 touches and 29.5 total yards. Last week, he played 63.3% of the snaps with 75.8% of the rushing work, and an 18.5% route share. Washington finished with 25 carries and 83 rushing yards. Washington has to run behind the same horrible offensive line that Jeanty does. Washington has managed a 12.3% explosive run rates nd 2.37 yards after contact per attempt, though. Washington's usage and volume are up in the air this week, but he has a horrible matchup incoming and is best left on the bench. Over their last five games, the 49ers have allowed the lowest explosive run rate, the second-lowest yards after contact per attempt, and the seventh-lowest missed tackle rate.

Since Week 3, Michael Mayer has been the TE9 in fantasy points per game. In those six games, Mayer has had a 13.3% target share, 1.83 YPRR, only two deep targets, one red zone target, and an 11.9% first-read share. He has been efficient with limited volume and doesn't have much high cholesterol usage in this offense. Even if I could get past all that, he has a tough matchup this week. The 49ers have been tough on tight ends. Over their last five games, they have allowed the fifth-fewest yards per target and the tenth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity. Sit Mayer.

Dalton Schultz is the TE18 in fantasy points per game, but that ranking is really just carried by his outing against Cincy. Schultz hasn't had double-digit PPR points in any other game this season. Schultz has a 57% snap rate, a 62.1% route share, a 17.7% target share with 1.91 YPRR, five red zone targets, four deep targets, and an 18% first-read share. Schultz is on the streaming radar this week. Across their last five games, the Bolts have allowed the most yards per target to tight ends while giving up the 13th-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Ok, well, here we go. I'm doing the Tyler Higbee thing again. There's no way that this backfires, right? (Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen say hi) Since Week 3, Higbee has been the TE21 in fantasy points per game. In his last three games, he has failed each week to surpass five PPR points. This is after three strong games in a row in Weeks 3-5. Since Week 3, he has had a 12.6% target share with 1.47 YPRR, two red zone targets, and a 15% first-read share. Higbee is a solid streaming option again this week (crossing my fingers). Over their last five games, Washington has allowed the sixth-most yards per target and the fifth-most fantasy points per opportunity.

With Bhayshul Tuten active, Chris Rodriguez could still see an elevated role this week. Rodriguez has had a 24.3% snap rate while averaging 6.7 touches and 33.2 total yards. Among 45 qualifying rushers, Rodriguez is 20th in yards after contact per attempt and 15th in missed tackle rate. Rodriguez is a touchdown-dependent flex. Baltimore hasn't been an easy team to run on. Over their last five games, Baltimore has allowed the second-lowest explosive run rate, the seventh-lowest rushing success rate, and the sixth-lowest yards after contact per attempt, but there is a sliver of hope here. Over the same time span, this run defense has also had the fourth-lowest rate of hitting backs at or behind the line of scrimmage, and it has allowed the 11th-highest gap rushing success rate (Rodriguez 53.3% gap).

With Jaylin Noel's injury and Houston coming off a bye, I'm expecting Marvin Harrison Jr.s snap rate to increase. In his first two games as a Texan, he had only a 19.5% snap rate, a 24.6% route share, 50% TPRR, 2.50 YPRR, two red zone targets, two deep targets, and a 17.1% first-read share. With his playing time up in the air and a middling matchup, Harrison Jr. is only a middling flex this week. Over their last five games, the Bolts have ranked 18th in yards per target and 16th in fantasy points per opportunity against perimeter wide receivers.

AJ Barner is a low-end tight end streaming option this week. It's all based on the matchup. Barner has a 12.3% target share with 0.96 YPRR, seven red zone targets, and a 13.7% first-read share. Barner is the TE27 in fantasy points per game, with only one game this season with double-digit PPR points. Over their last five games, Arizona has allowed the 14th-most receiving fantasy points per game and fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Christian McCaffrey's hamstring isn't 100%. With McCaffrey operating at less than full health and a nice rushing matchup incoming, I wouldn't be surprised to see Kaelon Black see 12-15 carries against the Raiders. Black has seen at least 12 carries in two games this season while averaging 8.5 touches and 33.9 total yards per game. Black hasn't been impressive as a rusher with only a 7% explosive run rate and 7% missed tackle rate, but that might not matter this week. The Raiders' run defense has been that bad. Over their last five games, Las Vegas has allowed the highest explosive run rate, the highest rushing success rate, the most yards before contact per attempt, and the fifth-highest missed tackle rate.

Since Week 5, Kendre Miller has averaged 14.4 touches and 42.6 total yards. In those three games, he has had a 39.3% snap rate, 52.8% of the rushing workload, and a 15.2% route share (6.5% target share). He has operated as New Orleans' early down grinder. That role might serve him well this week. Since Week 5, he has posted a decent 10.4% explosive run rate and 16% missed tackle rate. Miller is a decent flex play this week if he can get into the endzone. The Browns have been bleeding out production to backs. Over their last five games, they have allowed the second-highest explosive run rate, the eighth-highest rushing success rate, and the second-highest yards after contact per attempt and missed tackle rate.

Cam Skattebo didn't practice until Friday of this week (hamstring). He only managed a limited session on Friday and has been listed as doubtful. I expect Skattebo to miss this week, which means Devin Singletary should operate as the Giants' workhorse this week.

Over the last two games, with Jonah Coleman leading the way, J.K. Dobbins has seen his role reduced. In those games, Dobbins has had a 22% offensive snap rate with 6.5 rushing attempts and 18 rushing yards per game. Dobbins is a low-end, touchdown-dependent flex until that changes. Over their last five games, Carolina has allowed the tenth-highest explosive run rate, the ninth-highest yards before contact per attempt, and the fourth-highest missed tackle rate.

In Weeks 4-8, Mark Andrews has been the TE34 in fantasy points per game. He had eclipsed six PPR points only once during that span. Since Week 4, he has had a 15.1% target share with 0.81 YPRR, six red zone targets, two deep targets, and a 16.8% first-read share. Volume and red zone equity haven't been the issue. Andrews just isn't doing anything with the opportunities. I think this week is more of the same. Sit Andrews. Over their last five games, the Jags have allowed the fewest yards per target and the third-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Last week, Brian Thomas Jr. remained a limited snap player with a 45.5% route share, an 11.8% target share, and a 20% first-read share. Yes, he caught a touchdown, but I'm not chasing that as a reason to plug him into a lineup this week. Since Week 3, Thomas has surpassed a 50% route share only once, and last week was the first time since Week 2 that he had even sniffed a target share in the double digits. Sit Thomas until the usage picks up.

Jordyn Tyson returned to practice this week. He managed only limited sessions all week and has been listed as questionable. Tyson could be active this week, but it's impossible to plug him into a lineup even if he is on the field. I doubt that New Orleans would immediately install him as a full-time player. As a limited-snap player this week, Tyson would be an easy sit if active.

Kyle Monangai could be back this week. Monangai didn't practice until Friday this week (thumb/toe). He has been listed as questionable. Monangai is the RB16 in fantasy points per game this season, averaging 16.3 touches and 90.8 total yards. Among 42 qualifying rushers, Monangai is ninth in explosive run rate, second in yards after contact per attempt, and sixth in missed tackle rate. I don't expect Chicago to load him up with volume this week, but he could still be a solid flex this week. Over their last five games, Tampa Bay has allowed the 13th-most yards after contact per attempt, the eighth-highest zone yards per carry, and the 13th-highest zone rushing success rate (Monangai: 70% zone).

I expect Tank Dell's playing time to increase with Jaylin Noel out for the rest of the season, but the question is how much. In his first game back, he ran only four routes while drawing one target. Dell isn't a viable fantasy option until his playing time increases.

Jake Ferguson sustained an ankle injury last week. He didn't practice until Friday of this week. He was a limited participant on Friday and has been listed as questionable. Last week, he played only four snaps. In the two games before that, his usage had begun to decline. In those games, he had a 54.1% snap rate, a 51.2% route share, a 4.9% target share, and only one first-read target. Ferguson's usage and playing time were already worrisome, but if he's active this week and playing through an injury, I don't see his snap rate improving. Sit Ferguson this week.
